items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think that was just the two of us.

ctx.x: He also recorded that with Abbey Lincoln.
That's right. I think that was just the two of us.

items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn't know Hank Jones. I knew who he was

ctx.x: How do you work together on albums sort of across -­

The way Max used to work with me. He would suggest people. He knows all these people. I don't know them. I didn't know Hank Jones. I knew who he was, but I'd never -- I didn't know Hank Jones. I never would have thought to call J.J. Johnson or Charlie Haynes or Pat Metheny. He really enhances my life. He says, "Now, what do you think about so and so?" And if I say, "No," he'll say, "Okay. What do you think about?" He doesn't try to run my life. He has great respect for the music, you know, and he helps us to…
Is this about as close to an ideal situation?
